title: After all those years, only a few came aboard.
subtitle: The flood begins and the ship is loaded
then: When Allah's command came, water burst from the face of the earth, even from places where fire is lit. Nuh was told to load pairs of each creature, his household, and the believers. {trap}His son and his wife were not among them{/trap}, for they did not believe. {idea}Only a few believed{/idea}, even after nine hundred and fifty years of calling.
now: You count followers, likes, attendance at the halaqa, and feel like a failure when the numbers are small. {idea}Nuh had a few after centuries{/idea}, and he was still a success in Allah's eyes. Faithfulness is not measured in crowds.
old: If only a few people respond, my effort was wasted.
new: Allah measures sincerity, not numbers; a few who truly believe were enough for Nuh's ship.
try: Thank one person who has stayed loyal to a good effort of yours, even if they are the only one.

title: In Allah's name it sails and in His name it stops.
subtitle: Beginning a journey with His name
then: As the believers boarded, Nuh told them the ship's {idea}sailing and anchoring were in the name of Allah{/idea}. Even while the wrongdoers were about to drown, he called his Lord {reward}Forgiving and Merciful{/reward}. Ibn Kathir notes this is why saying Allah's name at the start of affairs, and when boarding or riding, is encouraged.
now: You get into the car for the school run, start the laptop for a hard meeting, sit down for a job interview. You usually just go. {idea}Say His name first.{/idea} The start and the stop of your day are in His hands.
old: My plans and preparation are what carry me through.
new: Every start and every stop happens by Allah's name, so I begin with it.
try: Say Bismillah out loud each time you start the car or a trip today.

title: My son, come aboard with us.
subtitle: A father's last call across the waves
then: The ship moved through {trap}waves like mountains{/trap}, carried by Allah's protection. Nuh saw his son Yam, a disbeliever, standing apart. {idea}He called him one more time{/idea}: come aboard with us, do not be with the disbelievers.
now: Your teenager has stopped praying and closes the door when you knock. Your grown child no longer answers your texts about faith. {idea}Nuh still called.{/idea} Love keeps the invitation open, gently, until the very end.
old: Once my child has turned away, there is nothing left to say.
new: A loving parent keeps calling softly, right up to the last chance.
try: Send one warm, pressure-free message to a family member who has drifted away.

title: No mountain is high enough against Allah's decree.
subtitle: The son trusts a mountain instead of mercy
then: The son answered that {trap}he would climb a mountain and the water would not reach him{/trap}. He thought the flood could not cover the peaks. Nuh told him that on this day {reward}there is no protector from Allah's command except His mercy{/reward}. Then a wave came between them.
now: You have your own mountains: the savings buffer, the insurance policy, the connections, the clever exit plan. They are useful, but they are not where safety comes from. {reward}Mercy is the only real high ground.{/reward}
old: As long as I have a backup plan, I am safe.
new: My plans help, but only Allah's mercy truly protects me.
try: When you check your bank balance or plans today, add a short dua asking Allah for His mercy.

title: Earth, swallow. Sky, hold back. And it was done.
subtitle: The flood ends at one command
then: When the deniers had drowned, Allah {idea}commanded the earth to swallow its water and the sky to stop{/idea}. The water sank, the matter was settled, and the ship came to rest on Mount Judi. Mujahid said the other mountains rose proud that day but Judi humbled itself. {trap}It was said: away with the wrongdoing people.{/trap}
now: You are in the middle of your own flood: the divorce paperwork, the layoff, the long diagnosis. It feels endless. {idea}The One who started it can end it with a word.{/idea} Storms obey Him.
old: This hard season will go on forever.
new: Every flood ends when Allah says so, and He can settle my matter in a moment.
try: Write one hard thing you are going through on paper and make dua that Allah settles it with ease.

title: My Lord, my son is of my family.
subtitle: A grieving father brings his question to Allah
then: After the flood, Nuh called to his Lord about his son. Allah had promised to save his family, and {reward}Allah's promise is true{/reward}. So how had his son drowned? It was {idea}a question, asked with respect{/idea}, ending with: You are the most just of judges.
now: You are in the hospital corridor after the news, or at home after a loss that makes no sense. Questions burn inside you. {idea}Bring them to Allah{/idea}, in prayer, the way Nuh did: honest grief, with trust still in it.
old: Questioning what happened means my faith is weak.
new: I can bring my hardest questions to Allah, as long as I bring them with trust.
try: In your next sujood, tell Allah honestly about one loss that still hurts.

title: He is not of your family, his deeds were not good.
subtitle: Faith, not blood, makes the family Allah saves
then: Allah answered that the son {idea}was not among the family He promised to save{/idea}. The promise was for those of his family who believed. Ibn Abbas said he was truly Nuh's son but {trap}opposed him in deeds and intention{/trap}. Nuh was told not to ask for what he had no knowledge of.
now: You assume that because your parents were pious, or your family is known at the masjid, you are covered. {idea}No one inherits faith.{/idea} Your own deeds are what place you in the family Allah saves.
old: Coming from a good family keeps me safe.
new: Belonging to the believers is about my own deeds, not my family name.
try: Pick one good habit you have relied on your family for, like dua or Quran, and do it yourself today.

title: Forgive me, or I will be among the losers.
subtitle: Nuh accepts the answer and turns to repentance
then: A great prophet, just corrected by Allah. Nuh did not argue or justify. {idea}He sought refuge from asking what he had no knowledge of{/idea}, and said that unless Allah forgave him and had mercy on him, {reward}he would be among the losers{/reward}.
now: Your boss points out a mistake in the report, or your spouse tells you your words hurt. Your first reflex is to explain why you were right. {idea}Nuh just turned back.{/idea} A sincere "forgive me" is stronger than a clever defense.
old: When I am corrected, I need to explain my side.
new: When corrected, the noblest response is to accept it and ask for forgiveness.
try: Next time you are corrected today, say "you are right, I am sorry" before anything else.

title: Step down in peace, with blessings on you.
subtitle: A new beginning for Nuh and those after him
then: When the ship rested, Nuh was told to {reward}come down with peace and blessings{/reward}, on him and on nations from those with him. Muhammad bin Ka'b said every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection is included in that peace. {trap}Others would enjoy life for a time, then meet punishment.{/trap}
now: You moved to a new city, started over after a breakup, or walked out of the hospital after recovery. A new beginning. {reward}The same peace is offered to you{/reward}, if you step into it as a believer.
old: Peace and blessing were for prophets long ago, not for someone like me.
new: The peace given to Nuh reaches every believer after him, including me.
try: On your next fresh start, even a new week, begin it with a short prayer for peace and blessing.

title: You did not know this story. So be patient.
subtitle: Nuh's story told to strengthen the Prophet ﷺ
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that this story was {idea}news of the unseen{/idea}; neither he nor his people knew it before, so no one could say he learned it from them. He is told to be patient with his people's rejection and harm. {reward}The good end is for those with taqwa.{/reward}
now: You are the only one at work who will not fudge the numbers. You are the sibling who keeps the peace while others gossip. It feels like losing. {reward}The story is not over.{/reward} Nuh's story is told so you keep going.
old: If doing right is costing me now, maybe it is not worth it.
new: Patience is worth it, because the final outcome belongs to the mindful.
try: Pick one right choice that has been costing you, and keep it one more day with the words: the end is for taqwa.
